title.narrative: Prevention, protection, and assistance to vulnerable survivors of human trafficking in Ukraine, 2023

description.narrative:
Context: Full scale war in Ukraine has led to an increase in cases of human trafficking as detected by Caritas specialists in different regions of Ukraine. Caritas Ukraine staff have screened cases of sexual exploitation, labour exploitation, forced begging, domestic servitude, and forced involvement in criminal activities and armed conflict. In addition, the large number of Ukrainian refugees who surveys demonstrate intend to return home likely also include many individuals in vulnerable situations who have been exploited. In the experience of Caritas Ukraine, trafficking survivors rarely apply to Ukrainian state institutions like social services or the police, but often refer to non-governmental or church-based organizations like Caritas.
Programme overview: The goal of this project is to reduce number of human trafficking cases in the long term, to screen for survivors of human trafficking among the most vulnerable population in Ukraine, and to provide survivors with targeted reintegration assistance.
Key activities include: 1. Awareness raising activities in order to prevent future instances of human trafficking among the population. 2. Proactive screening and identification of the victims among the vulnerable population and delivery of comprehensive assistance to the survivors and their family members. 3. Knowledge and experience sharing in counter trafficking with different stakeholders.
